verse.text: “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

reflection.scripture: “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
reflection.observation: Jesus is inviting us to examine where we place our security and hope. Earthly treasures — money, status, possessions, even our carefully curated online personas — are temporary by nature. Moths, rust, and thieves represent the inevitable decay and loss that comes with anything we try to hold too tightly in this life. This isn't a condemnation of having nice things; it's a diagnosis of misplaced devotion. When our hearts are anchored to what can be taken away, we live in quiet anxiety. When they're anchored to what lasts, we find freedom.
reflection.application: Today, take a quiet inventory of where your energy and worry are actually going. Is there something you're clutching — a goal, a possession, a reputation — that has more of your heart than it should? Practice one small act of open-handedness: generosity, letting go of a comparison, or simply pausing before a purchase to ask 'Will this matter in eternity?'
reflection.prayer: Lord, You know the things I secretly treasure — the ones I don't even admit to myself. Help me loosen my grip on what fades and set my heart on what lasts. Teach me to invest in people, in kindness, in Your kingdom. Let my security rest in You alone. Amen.
